summary: Working notes for the commercial capacity review of the stability chambers, covering chamber occupancy by programme, reserved pull windows and the lead-time assumptions used when quoting new stability work. Informal working copy kept for the review meeting.

properties.title: Chamber capacity review
properties.subject: Commercial capacity review
properties.keywords: stability; chambers; capacity; pull windows; quoting

slides.title: Chamber capacity review
slides.subtitle: Westravelle Analytical Ltd | Commercial | GB working draft, November 2016

slides.title: 1 Why we are looking at this
bullets: Requests for long-term storage have come in faster than the chamber programme was planned for
Several quotes in the autumn were turned down or cut back because we could not confirm a chamber slot
Need a plain view of what is booked, what is reserved and what is free before the next round of quotes

bullets.text: Figures here are capacity and scheduling only; no study results are in this deck

slides.notes: Keep this out of the client folders. For Alice and Leon to look at before Thursday.

slides.title: 2 Occupancy by chamber

rows: Stability lots from two projects; no room for new lots until the 12 month pulls
Reserved for a protocol that has not yet started; ask Leon whether it is still on
Current lots pull out at the end of December
Booked by the method validation group in the same weeks as the cycling work

slides.notes: Loading status is from the chamber log as of last week. Not checked against the LIMS yet.

slides.title: 3 Pull windows
bullets: Pull points follow the protocol: they are not moved to suit a chamber
Pulls in the same week share a sample trip where possible
Late pulls are noted on the batch card with the reason
bullets_right: Chamber A pulls cluster at the year end, so new loading there is a poor idea before February
Chamber C has the most flexibility at present
Ask the stability coordinator before offering any start date that falls inside a pull window
slides.notes: Pull calendar is in the shared drive. This is my reading of it, so check against the original.

slides.title: 4 Lead-time assumptions
bullets: Quotes assume the standard lead time from the rate card, counted from signed protocol to first loading
Where a chamber is full, the quote assumes the next free slot and says so
Expedited starts are not offered for long-term storage

bullets.text: Do not promise a start date until the chamber log has been checked

bullets: Analytical capacity for the first pull is checked with the QC method validation lead, not assumed
slides.notes: Saira has the current analytical slots. Confirm before we quote anything with a start in the new year.

slides.title: 5 Open points
bullets: Is the Chamber B reservation still live
Whether the rate card lead time still matches what the labs can actually do
Who signs off a deviation from the standard lead time: Alice or the QA side
Whether the old chamber log entries from before 2011 are worth keeping in the summary at all
slides.notes: Paper records before the electronic archive are patchy, so anything older than 2011 is from memory and should be marked that way.

slides.title: 6 Next steps
bullets: Leon to confirm the Chamber B reservation and the Chamber C start
Saira to confirm analytical slots for the pulls that fall in January
Gareth to redraft the lead-time paragraph for the rate card

bullets.text: Circulate to Alice before the next quote review
